ANCHORS: article Methods, 'Response coding asked about emotions and feelings and the extent to which they were felt was from Very slightly or not at all (1) to Extremely (5) over the past week.' Instrument: Watson D, Clark LA, Tellegen A (1988) J Pers Soc Psychol 54(6):1063-1070 (ref 39), with Crawford & Henry 2004 (ref 38). Processing script data/stoyel_2021_disordered_eating.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/stoyel_2021_neg_affect/.
note: VARIANT: PANAS-20 Negative Affect subscale -- the paper says 'The ten negative items in the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)', and the 10 workbook adjectives (Distressed, Upset, Guilty, Scared, Hostile, Irritable, Ashamed, Nervous, Jittery, Afraid) are exactly Watson et al.'s 10 NA terms, in the instrument's own order; not PANAS-X (60) or I-PANAS-SF (5 NA). Time frame is the study's 'In the past week'. RIGHTS: applied instrument_rights_register.csv row 'Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)' (verdict ship, Watson/Clark/Tellegen); variant pinned as above, not re-derived. CODE DERIVATION: positional -- the script renames NEGAF<k>.<wave> columns, sorted by integer k within each wave, to item_{i+1}; k runs contiguously 1..10 in every wave, so item_k = NEGAF<k>. Header diff of shipped item_text against the workbook header at each position: 30/30 (10 items x 3 waves). Re-running the derivation over the raw workbook reproduces all 18234 live (id, wave, item, resp) cells exactly; see verify_stoyel_2021_neg_affect.R. SPLIT: the header's shared stem 'In the past week, I have felt...' is shipped once in instructions (ellipsis as printed, three periods) and the adjective alone in item_text; no other transcription change. OPTIONS: only the endpoints are printed by the study (1 'Very slightly or not at all', 5 'Extremely'), so option_text for resp 2-4 is left blank rather than filled from the canonical PANAS anchors (A little / Moderately / Quite a bit); the workbook stores numbers only, no value labels.
